name: Labrador Retriever
personalitySummary: Friendly, outgoing, and eager to please, with a steady temperament that makes it one of the most reliable family dogs.
requirementsSummary: Needs daily vigorous exercise and mental stimulation; prone to weight gain so diet needs monitoring; regular vet checkups for joints.

name: Golden Retriever
personalitySummary: Gentle, affectionate, and endlessly patient, a classic people-pleaser that bonds closely with the whole household.
requirementsSummary: Needs an active routine and weekly brushing to manage a thick double coat; benefits from early obedience training.

name: German Shepherd
personalitySummary: Confident, intelligent, and loyal, with a strong protective streak toward its family.
requirementsSummary: Needs a job to do — structured training and vigorous daily exercise — or it can become anxious or destructive.

name: French Bulldog
personalitySummary: Playful, affectionate, and easygoing, a low-key companion that's happiest close to its people.
requirementsSummary: Struggles in heat and humidity due to a short snout; needs climate-controlled environments and modest exercise; often has higher vet costs.

name: Poodle (Standard)
personalitySummary: Exceptionally smart and athletic, often more sensitive and eager to bond than its elegant looks suggest.
requirementsSummary: Coat needs professional grooming every 4-6 weeks; needs mental stimulation as much as physical exercise.

name: Beagle
personalitySummary: Curious, friendly, and nose-driven, a merry pack dog that gets along with almost everyone.
requirementsSummary: Prone to following scents and wandering off leash; a securely fenced yard and consistent recall training help a lot; famously vocal.

name: Dachshund
personalitySummary: Bold, clever, and stubborn in equal measure, with a big personality in a small body.
requirementsSummary: Long spine is prone to injury — avoid stairs/jumping and keep weight in check; benefits from consistent, patient training.

name: Yorkshire Terrier
personalitySummary: Feisty, affectionate, and surprisingly bold, forming intense bonds with its owner.
requirementsSummary: Silky coat needs daily brushing or a short trim; small size makes it fragile around very young children.

name: Boxer
personalitySummary: Playful and goofy well into adulthood, with a protective, patient streak around kids.
requirementsSummary: High energy needs a real outlet daily; short muzzle means some heat sensitivity; benefits from early socialization.

name: Siberian Husky
personalitySummary: Independent, athletic, and mischievous, bred to run and think for itself.
requirementsSummary: Needs serious daily exercise and secure fencing (notorious escape artists); heavy seasonal shedding; not a breed that reliably comes when called off-leash.

name: Cavalier King Charles Spaniel
personalitySummary: Sweet, sociable, and affectionate, happiest curled up with its favorite person.
requirementsSummary: Does poorly with long stretches alone; needs regular vet monitoring for heart health as it ages.

name: Shih Tzu
personalitySummary: Affectionate and outgoing, a companion breed through and through with a dash of stubbornness.
requirementsSummary: Long coat mats without daily brushing or a short 'puppy cut'; short muzzle needs cool, low-exertion conditions.

name: Border Collie
personalitySummary: Widely considered the most trainable dog breed — brilliant, intense, and always looking for a task.
requirementsSummary: Needs a serious daily job (sport, herding, structured training) or it will invent its own, often destructively; not a low-key household pet.

name: Chihuahua
personalitySummary: Bold and devoted to its chosen person, often wary of strangers and other animals.
requirementsSummary: Tiny and fragile around young kids or rough play; gets cold easily and often needs a sweater in cool weather.

name: Pug
personalitySummary: Comical, affectionate, and food-motivated, a natural entertainer that thrives on attention.
requirementsSummary: Sheds more than its short coat suggests; needs cool environments and portion control to avoid weight-related breathing issues.

name: Bulldog (English)
personalitySummary: Laid-back, dignified, and affectionate, content to spend most of the day near its people.
requirementsSummary: Very heat-sensitive and prone to breathing difficulty; skin folds need regular cleaning; often carries higher lifetime vet costs.

name: Australian Shepherd
personalitySummary: Smart, energetic, and work-driven, deeply bonded to its family and eager for a task.
requirementsSummary: Needs vigorous daily exercise and mental work; can develop herding-nipping habits without an outlet; thick coat sheds seasonally.

name: Great Dane
personalitySummary: A gentle giant — calm, affectionate, and surprisingly low-energy indoors despite its size.
requirementsSummary: Needs space and sturdy furniture; food and vet costs run high; short lifespan is an emotional consideration.

name: Boston Terrier
personalitySummary: Friendly, lively, and easygoing, nicknamed the 'American Gentleman' for its good manners.
requirementsSummary: Moderate heat sensitivity from a shortened muzzle; low grooming needs; does well in smaller homes.

name: Basset Hound
personalitySummary: Laid-back, affectionate, and famously stubborn, with a deep bay and a nose that leads the way.
requirementsSummary: Long ears need regular cleaning to prevent infection; prone to weight gain from its low exercise drive; training takes patience.

name: Domestic Shorthair
personalitySummary: Wide-ranging personality since it's a mixed background, but generally adaptable, affectionate, and low-drama.
requirementsSummary: Minimal grooming and generally robust health; benefits from scratching posts and some interactive play daily.

name: Maine Coon
personalitySummary: Gentle giants of the cat world — sociable, dog-like in loyalty, and famously good with families.
requirementsSummary: Long coat needs weekly brushing; large size means proportionally larger food and litter costs.

name: Siamese
personalitySummary: Vocal, social, and highly intelligent, often described as more dog-like in how closely it bonds.
requirementsSummary: Very people-oriented and can be vocal/demanding about attention; not a cat that thrives being left alone often.

name: Persian
personalitySummary: Calm, sweet, and dignified, happiest in a quiet, predictable home.
requirementsSummary: Long coat mats easily and needs daily brushing, often professional grooming; flat face can cause breathing and eye issues.

name: Ragdoll
personalitySummary: Famously docile and affectionate, known for going limp with contentment when held.
requirementsSummary: Indoor-only recommended due to its trusting nature; semi-long coat needs weekly brushing.

name: British Shorthair
personalitySummary: Easygoing and undemanding, affectionate on its own terms rather than a constant lap cat.
requirementsSummary: Tolerates alone time well; prone to weight gain so portion control matters; dense coat needs weekly brushing.

name: Sphynx
personalitySummary: Extroverted, mischievous, and people-obsessed, often described as more like a dog than a cat.
requirementsSummary: Hairless skin needs regular bathing and sun/cold protection; often needs sweaters in cool homes; not truly hypoallergenic (skin oils still shed dander).

name: Bengal
personalitySummary: Athletic, bold, and endlessly curious, with a wild-cat look and a high-drive personality to match.
requirementsSummary: Needs significant daily enrichment and vertical space or it gets destructive; not ideal for a quiet, low-activity household.

name: Abyssinian
personalitySummary: Energetic and inquisitive, always on the move and eager to investigate everything.
requirementsSummary: Needs daily play and vertical space to climb; gets bored (and mischievous) without enough stimulation.

name: Scottish Fold
personalitySummary: Sweet-natured and adaptable, known for its owl-like folded ears and calm demeanor.
requirementsSummary: The folded-ear trait is linked to a cartilage condition that needs monitoring; folded ears also need regular cleaning.

name: Russian Blue
personalitySummary: Gentle, reserved, and loyal to its people, often shy with strangers but deeply affectionate at home.
requirementsSummary: Produces less of the Fel d 1 allergen, making it a popular pick for mild allergy sufferers; prefers a calm, consistent routine.

name: Devon Rex
personalitySummary: Playful, mischievous, and deeply attached to its people — sometimes called a 'pixie' cat for its elfin look and energy.
requirementsSummary: Fine curly coat provides less insulation, so it's sensitive to cold; skin needs occasional gentle cleaning.

name: American Shorthair
personalitySummary: Easygoing, even-tempered, and low-maintenance, a sturdy all-around companion.
requirementsSummary: Very few special requirements beyond routine care; adapts well to most households and schedules.

name: Birman
personalitySummary: Sweet, sociable, and gentle, known for striking blue eyes and quiet devotion to its family.
requirementsSummary: Semi-long coat sheds but doesn't mat as easily as a Persian's; enjoys company and does best without long stretches alone.

name: Norwegian Forest Cat
personalitySummary: Independent but affectionate, a sturdy, weather-hardy breed with a calm, friendly streak.
requirementsSummary: Thick double coat sheds heavily in seasonal blowouts and needs weekly brushing; enjoys climbing so benefits from tall cat trees.

name: Holland Lop
personalitySummary: Friendly and easygoing, one of the more sociable rabbit breeds and popular with first-time owners.
requirementsSummary: Needs a spacious pen plus daily out-of-cage exercise time; unlimited hay and a consistent diet are essential to prevent GI issues.

name: Mini Rex
personalitySummary: Calm and velvety-soft (its coat is famously plush), generally gentle and easy to handle.
requirementsSummary: Short coat is low-maintenance but hard flooring can cause sore hocks — provide soft resting mats.

name: Netherland Dwarf
personalitySummary: Small, energetic, and can be skittish — often better suited to calmer households and gentle, patient handling.
requirementsSummary: Tiny size makes it easily startled and fragile around boisterous kids; needs a secure, enriched enclosure with hideouts.

name: Flemish Giant
personalitySummary: Docile and famously calm for a rabbit, often called a 'gentle giant' — can be very sweet with patient handling.
requirementsSummary: Needs a large enclosure well beyond standard hutch sizes and a bigger food budget than other rabbit breeds; heavy for kids to safely hold.

name: Lionhead
personalitySummary: Playful and affectionate, known for its distinctive mane of fur around the head.
requirementsSummary: Mane needs regular brushing to prevent matting and wool block; otherwise a fairly easygoing companion breed.

name: Guinea Pig
personalitySummary: Social and vocal, guinea pigs bond well with people and do best living with at least one same-species companion.
requirementsSummary: Needs a same-species friend (they're not solitary animals), a roomy cage, daily fresh vegetables, and a source of vitamin C.

name: Syrian Hamster
personalitySummary: Solitary and nocturnal — must be housed alone, most active at night, and generally low-interaction during the day.
requirementsSummary: Must live alone (Syrians are territorial); short lifespan is worth knowing upfront; needs a large wheel and deep bedding for burrowing.

name: Dwarf Hamster
personalitySummary: Fast, small, and can be nippy — better watched than handled by younger kids, more of an observation pet.
requirementsSummary: Very fast and hard to hold securely; can sometimes live in same-sex pairs but often best alone; escape-proof housing is a must.

name: Gerbil
personalitySummary: Curious, active, and generally sociable in pairs or small groups of the same sex.
requirementsSummary: Needs deep bedding for natural digging behavior and a same-sex companion; low odor compared to other small rodents.

name: Fancy Rat
personalitySummary: Highly intelligent and genuinely affectionate — often the most interactive and trainable of the small rodents.
requirementsSummary: Best kept in same-sex pairs or groups for social wellbeing; short lifespan; prone to respiratory issues in dusty bedding.

name: Budgerigar (Budgie)
personalitySummary: Cheerful, social, and surprisingly good talkers for their size — a great entry point into bird ownership.
requirementsSummary: Needs daily out-of-cage flight time and social interaction; happier in pairs, though a single bird bonds closely with people.

name: Cockatiel
personalitySummary: Affectionate and expressive, known for whistling and a crest that visibly signals its mood.
requirementsSummary: Long lifespan is a real commitment (often 15-20+ years); produces fine feather dust that can affect allergy sufferers; needs daily attention.

name: Canary
personalitySummary: A watch-don't-handle bird — prized for its song rather than interaction, generally not hand-tame.
requirementsSummary: Not meant to be held or cuddled; best for someone who wants birdsong and visual enjoyment over hands-on interaction; males sing more than females.

name: Green-cheeked Conure
personalitySummary: Playful and cuddly with a big personality — comparatively quieter than larger parrots but still a real handful.
requirementsSummary: Can nip when startled, so supervised interaction with young kids is safer; needs daily out-of-cage time and chew-safe toys.

name: African Grey Parrot
personalitySummary: Exceptionally intelligent — often compared to a young child cognitively — and deeply bonded but demanding of a companion.
requirementsSummary: Decades-long lifespan is a lifetime commitment across a household's changes; needs hours of daily mental engagement or develops stress behaviors like feather plucking; not a beginner bird.
